Synthetic waiting periods

A waiting period is the time you must hold a fictional health policy before you can claim benefits for some services. Waiting periods also apply when you upgrade to a higher level of cover.

Maximum waiting periods for hospital cover

TreatmentMaximum waiting period
Hospital psychiatric services, rehabilitation and palliative care2 months
Pre-existing conditions12 months
Pregnancy and birth12 months
All other treatment2 months
Accident and emergency ambulanceNone

Extras cover

Waiting periods for extras such as dental, optical and physiotherapy are set by each insurer. Common examples are two months for general dental and physiotherapy, six months for optical, and twelve months for major dental.

Changing insurers

If you move to another insurer with the same or lower level of cover, you should not have to serve waiting periods again for benefits you had already waited for.
